children: Volvo Car's third-quarter results were disappointing, landing substantially below already low expectations, Deutsche Bank analyst Nikita Papaccio writes. This was primarily driven by the ongoing challenging market environment in China, which was also the key reason for the withdrawal of full-year guidance earlier this month, Papaccio says. Looking to 2027, the company highlighted limited visibility given the highly dynamic market environment. "It expects continued volume headwinds, while operating leverage should improve through adjustments to production capacity," Papaccio says. The company also announced another cost-savings program, including the layoff of 2,500 white-collar employees, aimed at reducing overhead costs. The bank lowers its target price to 9 Swedish kronor from 13 kronor and reiterates its hold rating. Shares rise 0.4% to 10.74 kronor. (dominic.chopping@wsj.com)
